$comment: Section grammar for rcg recipe plan. Learned from Adits effects/auto/advance/recipes.js (the six Advance recipes) and mapped to rapidContentGen tools; three sections are added from Phases 2-4. Adits footage effects (ghost, glitch, mosh, pixel stretch, ink...) wait for the P6 footage-FX pre-pass, so each is replaced by what exists now: a grade, a white flash, kick shake, a shader or beat-flash words. Camera intensities are scaled down for 9:16 footage (Adits 180% crash zoom = 3.7x here). Schema: docs/recipes.md.

suspense-build.when: Before a drop, reveal or hard cut. The shot must feel like it is going somewhere while almost nothing happens.
suspense-build.note: The long quiet segment carries a slow push so it is never static; intensity only arrives on the last, shortest segment. Adits: adv_ghost + bnw, then signal_overload glitch; here: mono grade, then a flash.

beat-drop.when: The peak. Land it on an audible hit and keep it short: this is the loudest thing in the edit.
beat-drop.note: Adits locks glitch flashes to the track (glitch.speed 0) and speed-syncs 0.7-2.4x. Here: flash + impact on the downbeat, kick shake, and an audio speed ramp clamped at 1x (24 fps footage stutters below 1x). The impact (a -6.5 LUFS hit that sustains 1.7 s) sits at 0.14 because the drop usually carries a voice line (R5).

whip-montage.when: A rapid-fire run of shots. 6-14 back to back; never the same treatment twice in a row.
whip-montage.note: Alternating whip direction is what sells the montage as cut rather than random; keep each shot under about 1.2 s. Whips go out over the last 0.25 s of a shot and come back in over the first 0.25 s of the next (the R3 pattern at double speed, so sub-second shots do not spend their whole length whipping); every shot settles on a neutral frame.

reveal.when: Introducing a subject, a title moment, or coming out of a dark passage.
reveal.note: Start obscured, then open up. The clean segment at the end is the payoff: put no effect on it. Adits isolates dark then bright areas with ink and holographic effects; here the grade goes from dark-cold to warm.

cinematic-orbit.when: A sustained hero moment. Give it room (Adits says 8 s or more; 4+ s works for an intro) and let the 3D move do the work.
cinematic-orbit.note: Adits uses an anamorphic black-hole model in a cosmos environment. Here: an rcg three scene with orbit on layer a and crash zooms on the downbeats on layer b, audio-reactive.

cool-down.when: After a peak, and before the end. Lets the previous section land instead of fatiguing the viewer.
cool-down.note: Adits leaves a deliberate gap of plain video: silence is a tool. Here the second shot is a static shot with no grade change, and the music fades out over it.

card-flythrough.when: Showing several moments, products or photos in one beat-locked move; a gallery or a recap.
card-flythrough.note: Stills are cut from the footage (seeded picks) unless the job supplies images. Arrivals snap to downbeats; whooshes land their crest on each arrival. Keep punch for nearby cards.

title-card.when: A line of copy that must be read: a cold open, a promise, an end card.
title-card.note: Black card, centered in the safe box, slam or stagger-up title. Under 2 s it reads as punctuation; give 2-3 s for a sentence.
